label: def:wenzl-A-operator
title: Wenzl A-operator $A^\lambda_{\mu\nu}(I)$: the $(\mu, \nu)$-block of an interface generator
html:
Definition (Wenzl A-operator). Let \lambda \vdash n with n = n_1 + n_2, and let I = \sigma_{n_1} \in \mathbf{H}_n(q) be the inter-block interface generator joining \mathbf{H}_{n_1}(q) and \mathbf{H}_{n_2}(q). In the Wenzl 1988 Littlewood–Richardson decomposition of the restriction V_\lambda \downarrow_{\mathbf{H}_{n_1} \otimes \mathbf{H}_{n_2}}, the Wenzl A-operator A^\lambda_{\mu u}(I) is the (\mu, u)-block of I acting on the corresponding isotypic summand:

  A^\lambda_{\mu
u}(I) \;\in\; \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_
u)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu
u}},

where c^\lambda_{\mu u} is the Littlewood–Richardson coefficient.

The A-operator provides the operator-valued payload for Wenzl's Sub-lemma 2.1. It enables reading the matrix-entry pole order at q o 0 and accumulating per-peel contributions into the per-isotope binding tower.

The bilinear-system solver extracts matrix entries of A^\lambda_{\mu u}(I) at the substrate q_0. The \mathbf{H}_6 extract is full-rank. The \mathbf{H}_{9+} extracts are least-squares fits over the inner-test family. A universal A-operator remains an open problem.
